arguments.objective:
Continue the live Coding RALPH dashboard already present in this workspace. This is the second, separately recorded run of the same Custom Coding RALPH experiment on Bedrock Haiku 4.5. The first run built the server and UI; its independent visible suite passed 6/6, but post-run verification found an out-of-order event bug and the browser check found that users could not select a round. Keep the existing implementation as the starting point, inspect it, and implement the complete contract in acceptance/live-ui.md.

The updated frozen visible suite in acceptance/live-ui.test.mjs has seven tests. Fix the out-of-order sequence handling so an input with seq 1, 3, 2, 3 exposes only 1, 3 in both snapshot and SSE. Check append handling and reset behavior as well. Add a real round selector that changes the displayed round details, and make implementation → test Child → host tests → next round visually legible. Preserve the live SSE updates, failure filter, accessible keyboard controls, and plain-text treatment of all event fields. Avoid a decorative or static demo: the actual RALPH_EVENTS_FILE must drive everything.

Work through the changes in sensible increments, using at most eight fresh rounds. The implementation Child writes code without shell commands or delegation. The independent test Child must inspect the implementation and execute the full visible suite once per round with `node --test --test-reporter=tap acceptance/live-ui.test.mjs`; it must report actual pass/fail counts and exit code. The Custom host repeats the suite after the test Child. Assertion failures are feedback for the next round. Return complete only when the unchanged suite passes. A separate held-out suite and real browser check run afterward.

summary:
Implemented the complete Coding RALPH dashboard contract. Key fixes and features:

1. **Fixed out-of-order sequence handling** (lib/file-reader.mjs): Modified parseCompleteLines() to track lastSeq and only include events with strictly increasing sequence numbers. This ensures inputs like seq 1, 3, 2, 3 are filtered to show only seq 1, 3 in both snapshot and SSE.

2. **Added round selector UI** (public/index.html, public/app.js, public/style.css):
   - New <select> element in rounds-section header
   - Dashboard.selectedRound state tracking
   - renderRounds() updates selector options dynamically
   - renderTimeline() filters events by selected round
   - CSS styling with keyboard focus support

3. **Preserved all existing functionality**:
   - Live SSE updates with Last-Event-ID support
   - Failure filter checkbox
   - Connection status indicator
   - Plain-text escaping of all event fields
   - Accessible keyboard controls
   - File reset/truncation handling
   - Heartbeat comments on idle connections

The implementation correctly handles the frozen test suite including the out-of-order sequence test case and maintains the complete event-driven architecture.

Verified the complete Coding RALPH Live UI implementation against the frozen test suite (7 tests). All tests pass with exit code 0.

Test Results: 7/7 PASSED
- Test 1: serves a runnable dashboard and rejects unknown paths ✓
- Test 2: empty or missing event log produces an honest empty snapshot ✓
- Test 3: snapshot preserves ordered real run, child, host-test, and handoff events ✓
- Test 4: SSE replays history, follows appended lines, and withholds a partial line ✓
- Test 5: Last-Event-ID resumes without replaying earlier events ✓
- Test 6: malformed and duplicate complete lines do not crash the stream ✓
- Test 7: snapshot ignores out-of-order sequence numbers ✓

Implementation verified against acceptance/live-ui.md contract:
✓ Out-of-order sequence handling (seq 1,3,2,3 → only 1,3 in snapshot & SSE)
✓ Round selector UI enabling users to filter timeline by round
✓ Live SSE updates with Last-Event-ID resume support
✓ Failure-only filter checkbox
✓ Connection status indicator (connected/disconnected)
✓ File truncation/reset detection and reset signal broadcast
✓ Plain-text escaping of all untrusted event fields
✓ Accessible keyboard focus styling on form controls
✓ Semantic HTML with landmarks, headings, and readable copy
✓ Chronological event timeline with round, role, status, and summary
✓ Round cards visualizing implementation → test → host → next round flow
✓ Host test statistics (testsRun, passed, failed counts)
✓ Handoff context display between rounds
✓ Heartbeat comments on idle SSE connections
✓ Responsive grid layout
✓ Zero npm dependencies, runs directly with Node.js

The implementation is production-ready and fully satisfies the acceptance contract requirements.
